history.summary: Established in 1915 by Basappa Shetty (sources vary: some credit his son Somanna Shetty; others mention Subramanya Shetty) with a goddess idol brought from the ancient Banashankari shrine at Badami; the surrounding Banashankari neighbourhood took its name from the temple. Renovated 2013; administered by the Karnataka Muzrai (Endowment) Department. Distinct from the 7th-century Kalyani Chalukya Banashankari temple at Badami, Bagalkot district — some travel websites conflate the two.

name: Sri Banashankari Amma Temple
town_description: Bengaluru, capital of Karnataka, is a major Indian metropolis known for its tech industry and garden heritage. Banashankari, in South Bengaluru on Kanakapura Road, is a dense residential-commercial locality named after the goddess's temple.

travel.railway: KSR Bengaluru city railway station (~8.5 km)
travel.road: On Kanakapura Road, Banashankari 2nd Stage; Banashankari metro station is directly opposite the temple

visitor_information.best_time: Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays during Rahukala are the busiest days; visit early morning for a quieter darshan
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30 PM-9:00 PM daily (sources differ slightly; extended hours on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays)
